subtopics.title: VAT — the Tax Already Inside the Price

questions.question: A cooler box is quoted at R690,00 EXCLUDING VAT. Its VAT-inclusive price is:
A till slip total of R1 288,00 INCLUDES VAT. The amount before VAT is found by:
options: Dividing R1 288,00 by 1,15 to get R1 120,00
Multiplying R1 288,00 by 0,85 to get R1 094,80
Multiplying R1 288,00 by 1,15 to get R1 481,20

questions.question: The standard-rated part of the basket costs R172,50 including VAT. The VAT contained in it is:
Which set of items is ZERO-RATED, so that no VAT is charged on them?
options: Maize meal, milk and brown bread

subtopics.title: Discount — What Comes Off, and Off What

questions.question: A tracksuit marked R640,00 is reduced by 30%. The sale price is:
20% off the R640,00 tracksuit, followed by a further 10% off at the till, gives a final price of:
Why is '20% off then 10% off' NOT the same as 30% off?
options: The shop rounds the second discount down
The second discount is taken off the already-reduced R512,00, not off the marked R640,00, so the combined multiplier is 0,72 — a 28% discount
VAT is added between the two discounts

questions.question: 'Buy two, get one free' is equivalent to a discount of about:
options: 50%, because one of the two is free
25%, because you get a quarter more
66,7%, because two of three are paid for
33,3%, because you pay for two of three items

subtopics.title: Simple Interest — Growth in a Straight Line

questions.question: R4 500 is invested at 7,5% SIMPLE interest per year for 3 years. The interest earned is:
In a simple-interest calculation, eight months must be substituted as:
What makes interest 'simple' rather than compound?
options: It is calculated on the original amount every period, never on interest already earned
It is always a lower rate
It is only paid at the end of the investment

questions.question: R4 500 grows to R5 062,50 in 2 years under simple interest. The annual rate is:

subtopics.title: The Fridge Decision — Three Tools, One Answer

questions.question: A fridge marked R7 200,00 is on sale at 15% off. The sale price is:
Six months' simple interest on R6 500 at 6% per year is:
Waiting six months instead of buying on sale leaves the family:
options: Better off by R195, because interest was earned
Exactly even, because the two effects cancel
R885 worse off overall, and R505 short of the R7 200 marked price
R1 080 worse off, with no other effect

questions.question: Which set of habits is named as the mark-earning routine for this topic?
options: Round every step to the nearest rand and use estimates
Write the substitution, keep units and cents, round only at the end, and answer in a sentence
Work only in percentages and avoid rand amounts
Do all arithmetic mentally to save time

subtopics.title: The Till Slip at the Corner Shop

questions.question: When the shelf price of washing powder reads R92,00, that R92,00 is:
options: The price before VAT is added at the till
The price with VAT already included
The price excluding a 15% service charge

questions.question: The whole basket totals R374,50 with R202,00 of it zero-rated. The VAT on the slip is:
The 'glass of squash' comparison makes which point about VAT?
options: VAT is stirred into the price already, so you cannot find it by taking 15% of the full amount
VAT is added only to liquids
VAT must be paid separately at the till

subtopics.title: The Sale Sign That Says More Than It Gives

questions.question: If 30% comes off a price, the quickest single step is to multiply by:
Compared with a true 30% discount on R640,00, the '20% then 10%' sale costs the shopper:
The plain-language rule for chained percentages given in the lesson is:
options: Add the percentages, then convert to a decimal
The second percentage eats only what the first one left on the plate
Always apply the larger percentage last

questions.question: The price after 20% then 10% off R640,00 is R460,80. To recover the marked price you would:

subtopics.title: Money That Grows the Same Amount Every Year

questions.question: R4 500 at 7,5% simple interest pays the saver, in each of the three years:
options: A growing amount: R337,50, then R362,81, then R390,02
R337,50 every year — the same amount each time

questions.question: The closing balance after three years is:
Substituting 6 instead of 0,5 for six months would make the interest answer:
Why is buying the fridge on sale better than waiting six months for interest?
options: Because 6% is smaller than 15% as a number
Because interest is taxed and discounts are not
Because R1 080 of discount is far larger than R195 of interest — a net gain of R885 in actual rands
